description: Lazy Theta* finds short *any-angle* paths on a grid: chains of straight segments between cell centres at any angle, not only in 45-degree steps. Like Theta*, it runs A* over the eight grid moves with Euclidean lengths, and a cell may take the parent of the cell that generated it as its own parent. Lazy Theta* makes that link without a check. It checks *line of sight* (that the straight segment crosses no blocked cell) only once, when it expands the cell; if the check fails, the cell takes its cheapest expanded neighbour as parent. This needs far fewer line-of-sight checks than Theta* for paths of similar length, but the paths are not guaranteed to be shortest, and unlike Theta* not guaranteed to be no longer than the cheapest 8-connected path.

papers.authors: Alex Nash, Sven Koenig, Craig Tovey
papers.title: Lazy Theta*: Any-Angle Path Planning and Path Length Analysis in 3D

lineage.source: heuristic-search, src/grid/theta.rs: "Lazy Theta*: theta_star with far fewer line-of-sight checks"
